House rules for desk cover
New handlers should know how the first steps go

This page matters because the Companion Animal Travel Desk is where the trip starts for animals and their people. Your job is to keep the check-in steady, calm, and clear so passengers feel guided instead of rushed. Aurelia Skyways depends on you to notice small details, keep the tone friendly, and move each case along without fuss.

Start by greeting the traveler and looking over the booking with care. If the companion animal is present, watch its posture, breathing, and response to noise before you do anything else. Keep your voice low and your movements smooth. Do not crowd the carrier or reach in without a reason. If the animal seems uneasy, slow the pace and give the handler room to settle it. A calm start prevents trouble later.

When you review the travel setup, check the service notes, the cabin space, and any handoff needs at the counter. <<FACT F031>> Stay with the ordinary flow of the desk and keep your explanation plain. If the traveler asks for help, give short directions and repeat the key points once, not in a rush.

Some routes need extra attention because the pet area has its own layout and name. <<FACT F044>> Use the same clean language every time so the traveler can follow the process without confusion. If you need to involve a senior coordinator, do it early and do it quietly. Never guess, never bluff, and never make the animal wait while you search for confidence.

The best desk work is simple, steady, and humane. Remember to keep your hands calm, your words clear, and your focus on safe companion travel.
